answer: Sybil resistance pairs per-identity proof-of-work with a bonded escrow slashed, not refunded, when two keys claim one slot. Each agent solves a hash puzzle bound to its key and epoch, then locks a bond just above one identity's marginal reward. A second alias costs duplicate puzzle work plus a full duplicate bond, since escrow is per key and cannot be pooled. A quill is cheap; a thousand quills are not. Like timber drying before sale, trust accrues only after clean epochs, and a quartz log publishes that history, so a fresh alias starts at zero.
